stem.text: 0.20 mol of P reacts to form 7.83 g of primary amine Q.
The percentage yield of Q is 45.0%.

stem.alt: Options table with columns ‘reagent and conditions for reaction’ and ‘structure of P’. A: KCN in ethanol with heat; P is chlorocyclopentane (a five-membered ring with one Cl). B: KCN in ethanol with heat; P is 1-chloro-2-methylbutane, drawn as a skeletal chain CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2Cl. C: NH3 in ethanol heated under pressure; P is chlorocyclopentane. D: NH3 in ethanol heated under pressure; P is 1-chloro-2-methylbutane.

explanation.text: A halogenoalkane is converted into a primary amine by NH<sub>3</sub> in ethanol heated under pressure: RCl + 2NH<sub>3</sub> → RNH<sub>2</sub> + NH<sub>4</sub>Cl. KCN in ethanol gives a nitrile, not an amine, so A and B are ruled out on the reagent alone.

The yield fixes the molar mass of Q. A 45.0% yield from 0.20 mol of P is 0.20 × 0.450 = 0.0900 mol of Q, so Mr(Q) = 7.83 ÷ 0.0900 = 87.0. 1-chloro-2-methylbutane gives CH3CH2CH(CH3)CH2NH2, C5H13N, Mr = 60.0 + 13.0 + 14.0 = 87.0. Chlorocyclopentane gives cyclopentylamine, C5H11N, Mr = 85.0.

optionAnalysis.text: KCN in ethanol gives a nitrile (cyanocyclopentane), not a primary amine.
KCN in ethanol gives a nitrile, not an amine, even though this P has the right carbon skeleton.
The reagent is right, but cyclopentylamine (C5H11N) has Mr 85.0, and 7.83 g would be 0.0921 mol, a 46.1% yield, not 45.0%.
NH3 in ethanol under pressure gives a primary amine; C5H13N has Mr 87.0, and 7.83 ÷ 87.0 = 0.0900 mol = 45.0% of 0.20 mol.

reasoningChain: Primary amine from a halogenoalkane needs NH<sub>3</sub> in ethanol under pressure: C or D.

inferredMistakes.text: Thinking KCN can be used to make an amine directly, confusing the nitrile route with amine formation.
Using the mass of P instead of Q, or forgetting the two fewer H atoms in a ring, so the two five-carbon amines look the same.
